purpose: Extend the exact-congruence boundary diagnostic to the actual finite power-of-two Fourier output law on small synthetic cyclic groups.
state: Uniform a,b in [0,Q); third register f(a,b)=a+d*b mod r. Trace out the third register after two Q-point Fourier transforms.
probability: For each z, 2D FFT the indicator 1[f(a,b)=z]; sum squared amplitudes divided by Q^4. This is classical numerical state-law calculation, not a quantum run.
postprocessor: s=round(u*r/Q) mod r; t=round(v*r/Q) mod r; if s invertible propose d=t/s mod r. Invalid s rejected. Half-integer ties round upward. Nearest-character decoding is a bounded heuristic, not a complete recovery algorithm.
metrics: expected Euclid divisions per measured pair
controls: Compare FFT with naive complex DFT on length8
Check d=1 symmetry between Fourier registers
limitations: Small synthetic cyclic groups only, no elliptic-curve circuit or group-law timings
Floating-point amplitudes, not formal rational bounds
Candidate correctness checked against synthetic known secret; actual ECC verification still owed
No inference of cryptographic-size success probability
